plain.li: [lk:story,theirs,warmly,lk:lead] Let me tell you a story they tell at {TOWN}, because I cannot keep it to myself any longer.
[lk:story,warm|cordial,lk:lead] Since there is not much news, have a story instead. It is better than the news.
[lk:story,warm|cordial,lk:lead] Something happened here that you will not believe, so I will tell it slowly.
[lk:story,theirs,warm|cordial,lk:lead] Here is a tale they tell at {TOWN}. It might even be true.
[lk:story,theirs,warmly,lk:lead] Our oldest neighbour told this one at supper, and I have stolen it for you.
[lk:story,cordial|cool,lk:lead] I am not one for stories, but this one wants telling.
[lk:story,theirs,w:tribal,lk:lead] This is a story we tell at the fire when the nights are long. I give it to you the way it was given to me.
[lk:story,theirs,w:tribal,lk:lead] Sit, and I will tell it as the old ones tell it, with the parts they leave out left out.
[lk:story,theirs,w:spacer,lk:lead] Nothing much happens out here that would interest the feeds, but here is something that interested us.
[olde,lk:story,theirs,lk:lead] Hearken, for here is a tale of {TOWN}, and I tell it as it was told to me.
[olde,lk:story,lk:lead] Now I shall tell thee of a thing that befell us, and thou mayst judge it as thou wilt.
[olde,lk:story,warmly,lk:lead] Sit thee down by thy fire, friend, for this is a tale for a long evening.
[u:none,lk:story,lk:lead] Here is a story.
[u:none,lk:story,lk:lead] I will tell you what happened.
[sv:beast,lk:story,lk:lead] Here is a hunt-tale. Read it slowly, the way a trail is read.
[sv:ancient,lk:story,lk:lead] Permit me a tale from my earlier centuries. I have trimmed it to the essentials, which took some decades.
[lk:story,lk:after,theirs] Anyway. That is the news from {TOWN}, more or less.
[lk:story,lk:after] Make of that what you will. We still have not.
[lk:story,lk:after] Nobody here agrees on what it means, which is half the pleasure of it.
[lk:story,lk:after,warmly] I have told it badly, but you will forgive me, and tell it better yourself.
[lk:story,lk:after,w:tribal] That is how it was told to me. Now it is yours to tell.
[olde,lk:story,lk:after] Make of it what thou wilt; we are debating it at the well yet.
[u:none,lk:story,lk:after] That's the story.
[lk:raid,rd:now,theirs,lk:lead] You will have heard rumours on the road. Here is what really happened.
[lk:raid,rd:now,rd:fresh,theirs,lk:lead] Raiders came at us not ten days ago, and I want you to hear it from me before you hear it from the road.
[lk:raid,rd:now,rd:recent,theirs,lk:lead] It is a few weeks now since the raiders came. The town talks about it less than it did, but it still talks.
[lk:raid,rd:now,rd:past,theirs,lk:lead] It is long enough since the raid that we can speak of it without shouting, so I will.
[lk:raid,rd:now,rd:end:ongoing,theirs,lk:lead] I am writing this with raiders still about, so forgive the hand, which is not steady.
[lk:raid,rd:now,rd:road,theirs,lk:lead] There has been trouble on our roads, and you should know of it, since you use them too.
[lk:raid,rd:now,rd:you,theirs,lk:lead] You know what you did. I will tell you how it looked from our side of the wall.
[lk:raid,rd:now,rd:helped,theirs,lk:lead] Your people stood on our walls when it mattered. Here is the whole of it, for those of yours who were not there to see.
[lk:raid,rd:old,theirs,lk:lead] There has been no raid here in years, thank the weather, but the old ones still tell of the last, and so will I.
[lk:raid,rd:old,lk:lead] When I was small, the raiders came. I have never written it down before.
[lk:raid,rd:old,lk:lead] My grandmother told this one, and her mother before her, and now it is my turn.
[lk:raid,rd:old,cordial|cool,lk:lead] You live on a road, as we do, so you might as well hear what the road can bring.
[lk:raid,rd:old,w:tribal,lk:lead] It was long ago, before my mother had her name. I will tell it as it is told at the fire.
[lk:raid,rd:now,w:tribal,theirs,lk:lead] The raiders came. I will tell it the way it is told at the fire, though it is too new to be a fire-story yet.
[lk:raid,rd:boast,lk:lead] You will remember us. We remember you.
[lk:raid,rd:boast,lk:lead] In case anyone at your place has forgotten how it went, here it is again.
[lk:raid,ours,rd:ours,lk:lead] We had raiders here. Everyone is all right who can be, and I wanted you to hear it from us.
[lk:raid,ours,rd:ours,lk:lead] It has not been quiet here, and since you would hear of it anyway, here it is.
[olde,lk:raid,rd:now,theirs,lk:lead] Hear now how the reavers came upon {TOWN}, for it is fit that thou shouldst know it.
[olde,lk:raid,rd:old,theirs,lk:lead] In the days of my grandsire the reavers came, and the tale is told yet at {TOWN}.
[olde,lk:raid,rd:now,rd:helped,theirs,lk:lead] Thy people stood upon our walls in the hour of need, and I would have thee know the whole of it.
[olde,lk:raid,rd:now,rd:you,theirs,lk:lead] Thou knowest well what thy people did. Hear now how it seemed from within our walls.
[olde,lk:raid,ours,rd:ours,lk:lead] Reavers came upon us, and I would have thee hear it from mine own hand.
[sv:machine,lk:raid,rd:now,lk:lead] INCIDENT REPORT FOLLOWS. COMPILED FROM WITNESS ACCOUNTS AND OWN SENSORS.
[sv:machine,lk:raid,rd:old,lk:lead] HISTORICAL INCIDENT FOLLOWS, FROM ARCHIVE. ACCURACY: AS RECORDED, WHICH IS TO SAY UNKNOWN.
[sv:beast,lk:raid,lk:lead] The raiders came on the wind. We smelled them first. Here is how it went.
[u:none,lk:raid,rd:now,lk:lead] We had a fight.
[u:none,lk:raid,rd:old,lk:lead] My grandad told me this.
[u:none,lk:raid,rd:boast,lk:lead] You remember us. We remember you.
[lk:raid,lk:after,rd:now|rd:old] That is all of it. Bar your gate at night.
[lk:raid,lk:after,rd:now] I would not have written it if I did not think you should know.
[lk:raid,lk:after,rd:boast] Think on that, next time.
[olde,lk:raid,lk:after] May thy walls be better kept than ours were.
[sv:machine,lk:raid,lk:after] END OF INCIDENT REPORT. RECOMMENDATION: VIGILANCE.
[lk:poem,warm|cordial,lk:lead] I have been trying my hand at verse again. Be kind, or at least be quiet about it.
[lk:poem,warmly,lk:lead] Someone here wrote this, and I copied it out for you because it made me think of you.
[lk:poem,theirs,warm|cordial,lk:lead] Forgive me what follows. It is a song we sing here, and I could not get it out of my head.
[lk:poem,warm|cordial,lk:lead] Here are a few lines. I am no poet, but the evenings are long.
[lk:poem,cordial|cool,lk:lead] I enclose some verse, since it says it better than I would.
[lk:poem,condolences,lk:lead] I could not find the right words of my own, so here are some that have been said before.
[lk:poem,theirs,w:tribal,lk:lead] This is a song we sing. Sing it if you like; it does not mind who sings it.
[lk:poem,ours,warm|cordial,lk:lead] I have been writing a little verse in the evenings. Here is some of it, for better or worse.
[olde,lk:poem,lk:lead] I have set down some few lines in verse, and pray thou wilt forgive the rhymes.
[olde,lk:poem,theirs,lk:lead] Here is a song of our country, which the young folk sing at harvest and the old folk sing all year.
[olde,lk:poem,condolences,lk:lead] I have no fit words of mine own, so here are older ones.
[u:none,lk:poem,lk:lead] I made a poem.
[u:none,lk:poem,lk:lead] Here's a song my mam sang.
[sv:fey,lk:poem,lk:lead] A song, which is also the formula. Sing it back and the formula is closed.
[sv:green,lk:poem,lk:lead] A slow song, as we sing them. Read it in the morning, when it is warmest.
[sv:machine,lk:poem,lk:lead] ATTEMPT AT VERSE FOLLOWS. CONFIDENCE: LOW.
[sv:ancient,lk:poem,lk:lead] A verse in a form no longer in use. I have rendered it into your speech, imperfectly, as one must.
[lk:poem,lk:after,warm|cordial] There. It is out of my head now and into yours.
[lk:poem,lk:after] I will not ask what you thought of it.
[lk:poem,lk:after,warmly] If it made you smile, it did its work. If not, use it to light the fire.
[olde,lk:poem,lk:after] There, I have done, and thou mayst laugh.
[sv:machine,lk:poem,lk:after] END OF VERSE. IT IS SHORTER THAN IT FELT.
[lk:sermon,lk:lead] Bear with me, for there are things that must be said, and I am the one to say them.
[lk:sermon,warm|cordial,lk:lead] You will forgive me if I speak of the faith. I cannot help it, and I would not if I could.
[lk:sermon,theirs,lk:lead] I copied out what was preached here at the last gathering, because you ought to hear it.
[lk:sermon,lk:lead] There is something I must tell you, and it is bigger than either of us.
[lk:sermon,zeal:crank,lk:lead] They tell me nobody wants to hear it. That is how I know it must be said.
[lk:sermon,zeal:crank,lk:lead] I have written to everyone about this. You are the first to be written to twice.
[lk:sermon,ours,lk:lead] Forgive me a little preaching. It is on my mind, and you are a patient reader.
[olde,lk:sermon,lk:lead] Suffer me to speak of holy things, for my heart is full of them.
[olde,lk:sermon,theirs,lk:lead] Hear now what was preached at {TOWN} at the last gathering, for it was well said.
[u:none,lk:sermon,lk:lead] I have to tell you something important.
[sv:deep,lk:sermon,lk:lead] Listen. Not with the ears.
[lk:sermon,lk:after] There. I feel better, and I hope that you do.
[lk:sermon,lk:after,zeal:crank] Burn this if you like. It will still be true.
[olde,lk:sermon,lk:after] Ponder it, and may it do thee good.
[lk:chronicle,theirs,w:industrial|w:spacer,lk:lead] I enclose the latest sheet from town, which says everything I would and some things I would not.
[lk:chronicle,theirs,w:industrial|w:spacer,lk:lead] Our newsletter goes out to everyone now, so you may as well have a copy too.
[lk:chronicle,theirs,w:spacer,lk:lead] The bulletin came over the wire this morning. Here it is, as printed.
[lk:chronicle,theirs,empire,lk:lead] The gazette of the court, as issued this quarter, for your information.
[lk:chronicle,theirs,w:tribal,lk:lead] This is the season as it was told at the fire on the last night of it.
[olde,lk:chronicle,theirs,lk:lead] Here are the tidings of {TOWN}, as they were cried in the market.
[sv:machine,lk:chronicle,lk:lead] LOCAL STATUS DIGEST APPENDED.
[sv:hive,lk:chronicle,lk:lead] The many have counted the season. Here is the count.
[lk:petition,theirs,lk:lead] The town asked me to send this with my letter, and I could hardly refuse.
[lk:petition,theirs,!w:tribal,lk:lead] We put this together at a meeting, and everyone who could hold a pen signed it.
[lk:petition,theirs,w:tribal,lk:lead] We sat in a circle and said what we wanted, and here it is, with all our marks.
[lk:petition,ours,lk:lead] We talked it over at supper, and everyone signed.
[olde,lk:petition,theirs,lk:lead] The good folk of {TOWN} have set their names to this, and bid me send it.
[u:none,lk:petition,lk:lead] Everyone signed this.
[lk:account,lk:lead] So that there is no confusion, here it is set out plainly.
[lk:account,m:trade,lk:lead] A short account, since I know you like to see the numbers.
[lk:account,k:request,lk:lead] Here is the list of what we need, so you can see it is not much.
[olde,lk:account,lk:lead] Here followeth the reckoning, set down plainly.
[sv:machine,lk:account,lk:lead] INVENTORY APPENDED.
[u:none,lk:account,lk:lead] I wrote a list.
[lk:recipe,theirs,lk:lead] Here is something to do with whatever is left in your pantry.
[lk:recipe,theirs,warmly,lk:lead] My grandmother's recipe, which I am not supposed to give anyone, so please do not tell her.
[lk:recipe,theirs,help,medicine,lk:lead] We cannot send medicine, but here is what we do instead, and it is better than nothing.
[lk:recipe,ours,lk:lead] This is how {COOK} makes it here. I stood at the stove and wrote it down.
[olde,lk:recipe,theirs,lk:lead] Here is how we make it at {TOWN}, and thou wilt thank me for it.
[olde,lk:recipe,theirs,help,medicine,lk:lead] We have no physic to spare, but here is what the wise-wives do, and it hath served us.
[lk:riddle,lk:lead] A riddle, to keep you busy until my next letter.
[lk:riddle,theirs,lk:lead] Here is one the children here have been asking everyone.
[lk:riddle,lk:lead] I will not tell you the answer until next time. I am cruel that way.
[lk:riddle,theirs,w:tribal,lk:lead] We tell this one at the fire to make the young ones quiet. It works for a while.
[olde,lk:riddle,lk:lead] Here is a riddle for thee, and the answer in my next.
[sv:fey,lk:riddle,lk:lead] A riddle, which you must answer or not, as you like. We will know either way.
[sv:ancient,lk:riddle,lk:lead] A riddle from a court that no longer stands. It was considered easy there.
[lk:diary,lk:lead] I have been keeping a diary, and copied out a page of it for you, since it says more than I would.
[lk:diary,lk:lead] Here are a few days from my journal, as they were written.
[lk:diary,warmly,lk:lead] I write a little every night. Here is what this week looked like, more or less.
[olde,lk:diary,lk:lead] I have copied out some days from my book, that thou mayst see how we live.
[sv:ancient,lk:diary,lk:lead] Some entries from my journal, from the last few days. You will find them dull. So did I, and I have had practice.
[lk:story,lk:lead,fam:familiar|fam:close] You know me well enough by now to know I cannot write a letter without a story in it. Here is this one's.
[lk:story,lk:lead,fam:new,theirs] Since we do not know each other yet, let me tell you a story of {TOWN}; it will tell you more than I could.
[lk:poem,lk:lead,fam:familiar|fam:close] You have put up with my verses before, so here is another.
[lk:poem,lk:lead,fam:new] I hope you will forgive a stranger a verse.
[lk:recipe,lk:lead,fam:familiar|fam:close] I have been meaning to send you this for a long while. Here it is at last.
[lk:riddle,lk:lead,fam:familiar|fam:close] A riddle, because you strike me as someone who likes one, and because I have run out of excuses not to.
[lk:diary,lk:lead,fam:close] I am sending you a page of my days, because you are the one person who would read it.
[olde,lk:story,lk:lead,fam:familiar|fam:close] Thou knowest me well enough to know I cannot write a letter but there be a tale in it. Here is this one's.
[lk:story,lk:after,fam:familiar|fam:close,theirs] There. Now you know one more thing about us than anyone outside {TOWN} does.
[lk:poem,lk:after] That is all of it. It is better read aloud, if you can bear to.
[lk:sermon,lk:after] I have said my piece. I will not say it again unless you ask.
[lk:raid,lk:after,rd:now,theirs] I have written it down so that it is written somewhere outside {TOWN}. Keep it.
[lk:chronicle,lk:after] That is the news. The sheet will be wrong about some of it, as always.
[lk:recipe,lk:after] If it goes wrong, it is the oven. It is always the oven.
[olde,lk:poem,lk:after] There, that is all of it. It is better sung, if thou canst bear it.
[lk:raid,rd:now,rd:road,theirs,lk:lead] Our road has been dangerous lately, and you should know how dangerous, since your letters travel it.
[lk:raid,rd:now,rd:you,theirs,lk:lead] I will not shout. I will only tell you what it was like on the other side of your attack.
[olde,lk:raid,rd:now,rd:road,theirs,lk:lead] There hath been trouble upon our roads, and thou shouldst know it, for thy letters travel them.
[lk:story,lk:lead,w:tribal] This is a story the old ones tell when the fire is low. I tell it to you now.
[lk:poem,lk:lead,w:tribal] Here is a song of ours. Sing it at your fire, if you have one.
[lk:chronicle,lk:lead,w:tribal] Here is our season, as it was told at the fire.
[lk:recipe,lk:lead,w:tribal] The grandmother says I must send you this, so here it is.
[lk:riddle,lk:lead,w:tribal] The children made me promise to send you a riddle.
[lk:diary,lk:lead,w:tribal] Here are some of my days, as I would tell them at the fire.
[olde,lk:poem,lk:lead] I have made some verses, and thou shalt have them whether thou wilt or no.
[olde,lk:sermon,lk:lead] Bear with me, friend, for I would speak of holy things.
[olde,lk:recipe,lk:lead] Thou didst never ask, but here is how we make it.
[olde,lk:riddle,lk:lead] Here is a riddle to pass a winter's night.
[olde,lk:diary,lk:lead] I send thee some pages of my days, such as they are.
[olde,lk:chronicle,lk:lead,theirs] Here followeth the crier's roll of {TOWN}, as it was cried this quarter.
[olde,lk:account,lk:lead] Here is the reckoning, set down fair.
[olde,lk:petition,lk:lead,theirs,k:request] The folk of {TOWN} have set their names to this, and I send it on.
[lk:chronicle,lk:lead,w:spacer] Attaching this cycle's bulletin, printed, since I know you prefer paper.
[lk:diary,lk:lead,w:spacer] Attaching some log entries. Personal ones. Do not tell anyone I keep a personal log.
[sv:machine,lk:recipe,lk:lead] ATTACHED: ONE (1) PROCEDURE. HUMANS REPORT IT AS PLEASANT.
[sv:machine,lk:diary,lk:lead] ATTACHED: EXCERPTS FROM THIS UNIT'S LOG, SELECTED FOR RELEVANCE AND, THIS UNIT IS TOLD, CHARM.
[sv:machine,lk:riddle,lk:lead] QUERY FOLLOWS. YOU MAY ATTEMPT AN ANSWER.
[sv:green,lk:poem,lk:lead] We grew you a song.
[sv:green,lk:recipe,lk:lead] You asked nothing, but we will tell you how we eat.
[sv:beast,lk:recipe,lk:lead] You two-legs like to know how things are eaten. Here.
[sv:beast,lk:diary,lk:lead] Some of our days, by nose.
[sv:hive,lk:poem,lk:lead] The many made a hum for you.
[sv:hive,lk:sermon,lk:lead] The many believe. Here is how.
[sv:deep,lk:riddle,lk:lead] A question, from below.
[sv:deep,lk:poem,lk:lead] A song we heard through the floor of the world.
[lk:story,lk:lead,empire] A story of the court, which I may tell you because it is not mine.
[lk:poem,lk:lead,empire] A piece of court verse, as it is sung at the long table when the wine has gone round.
[lk:diary,lk:lead,empire] A page of my days at court, which are less splendid than you might imagine.
